import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set the figure size
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Create a bar chart for the survival rate based on class
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
sns.countplot(x='pclass', hue='survived', data=data)
plt.title('Survival Rate by Class')
plt.xlabel('Class')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='Survived')

# Create a histogram for the age distribution
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
sns.histplot(data['age'], kde=True)
plt.title('Age Distribution')
plt.xlabel('Age')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')

# Layout so plots do not overlap
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set the figure size
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Create a bar chart for the survival rate based on class
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
sns.countplot(x='pclass', hue='survived', data=data)
plt.title('Survival Rate by Class')
plt.xlabel('Class')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='Survived')

# Create a histogram for the age distribution
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
sns.histplot(data['age'], kde=True)
plt.title('Age Distribution')
plt.xlabel('Age')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')

# Layout so plots do not overlap
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
